source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN Examination, 7th ed.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: During the preoperative interview, which information should the nurse report to the anesthesiologist as a risk factor for malignant hyperthermia?
options: The client had heat stroke after a fun run last year
The client's brother developed a very high fever during general anesthesia
The client is allergic to shellfish and iodine
The client takes paracetamol for occasional headaches
questions.rationale: Malignant hyperthermia is an inherited reaction to certain anesthetic agents (succinylcholine and inhalation agents). A family history of problems with general anesthesia is the key risk finding.
explanations: Heat stroke is an environmental heat illness, not a genetic reaction to anesthetics.
Correct: a relative's anesthesia reaction suggests an inherited susceptibility.
Relevant to contrast media, not to malignant hyperthermia.
Paracetamol use has no link to malignant hyperthermia.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 192)
questions.quote: Questioning the client about the family history of general anesthesia problems may reveal this as a risk for the client.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client is on the first postoperative day after an open abdominal surgery and has a nasogastric tube to low suction. The nurse hears no bowel sounds. What should the nurse do?
options: Give sips of water to stimulate peristalsis
Clamp the nasogastric tube for one hour
Notify the surgeon of a paralytic ileus
Document the finding and keep reassessing
questions.rationale: Handling of the bowel during surgery commonly stops peristalsis for 3 to 4 days. Absent bowel sounds on day 1 is expected; the nurse documents and continues to monitor, and the client stays NPO with the NGT in place.
explanations: Oral intake is withheld until bowel sounds return.
The NGT is not clamped or removed without a prescription.
Absent bowel sounds on day 1 is an expected finding, not an emergency.
Correct: this is expected after bowel manipulation; continue monitoring.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 454)
questions.quote: Bowel sounds may be absent for 3 to 4 postoperative days because of bowel manipulation during surgery.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: On the third day after a hysterectomy, the client complains of pain in her right calf. What is the nurse's MOST appropriate action?
options: Check the calf for warmth, redness, and swelling
Massage the calf gently to relieve the cramp
Walk the client in the hallway to ease the pain
Give the PRN analgesic and reassess in 30 minutes
questions.rationale: Calf pain after pelvic surgery may signal deep vein thrombosis. The nurse first assesses the calf; massaging or ambulating could dislodge a clot, and giving an analgesic skips needed assessment.
explanations: Correct: assess for signs of DVT before any other action.
Massage can dislodge a thrombus and cause an embolism.
Ambulation can also dislodge a thrombus.
Pain relief before assessment may mask a serious complication.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 156)
questions.quote: Pain in the calf area could indicate a deep vein thrombosis.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: The nurse is helping a client cough and deep breathe after a thoracic surgery. Which item will make these exercises MOST effective?
options: A pillow to splint the incision
questions.rationale: Splinting the incision with a pillow reduces pain during coughing, so the client can breathe deeply and cough more effectively.
explanations: A nebulizer delivers medication; it does not support coughing.
Suction is for clients who cannot clear secretions themselves.
Correct: splinting reduces incisional pain so coughing is effective.
A resuscitation bag is for assisted ventilation in emergencies.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 418)
questions.quote: The client who is comfortable will do more effective deep breathing and coughing exercises.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.situation: Mang Ramon, a 45-year-old tricycle driver, is admitted after a road crash with blunt chest trauma. A chest tube is inserted in the emergency room, and he is transferred to the surgical ward.
questions.stem: Over the next 24 to 48 hours, which finding is the EARLIEST sign that Mang Ramon may be developing acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS)?
questions.rationale: ARDS usually appears 24 to 48 hours after the injury. Tachypnea and dyspnea come first as the body compensates for mild hypoxemia; cyanosis, crackles, and x-ray changes appear later.
explanations: Cyanosis is a late sign of severe hypoxemia.
Correct: tachypnea is the earliest compensatory sign.
Breath sounds are usually clear early, then crackles develop.
Chest x-ray findings may be normal in the early stage.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 162)
questions.quote: In most cases, tachypnea and dyspnea are the earliest clinical manifestations

questions.subject: NP III
questions.situation: Mang Ramon, a 45-year-old tricycle driver, is admitted after a road crash with blunt chest trauma. A chest tube is inserted in the emergency room, and he is transferred to the surgical ward.
questions.stem: When redressing the chest tube insertion site, which material should the nurse apply as the FIRST layer?
questions.rationale: Petrolatum gauze is placed directly on the site to make an occlusive seal that prevents air leaks. Gauze layers go on top, secured with strong tape.
explanations: Dry gauze is added over the first layer but does not seal the site.
An antiseptic-soaked layer does not create an airtight seal.
Transparent film does not seal around the tube itself.
Correct: petrolatum gauze creates an occlusive seal.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 485)
questions.quote: The first layer of the chest tube dressing is petrolatum gauze, which allows for an occlusive seal at the chest tube insertion site.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.situation: Mang Ramon, a 45-year-old tricycle driver, is admitted after a road crash with blunt chest trauma. A chest tube is inserted in the emergency room, and he is transferred to the surgical ward.
questions.stem: Mang Ramon later develops a pleural effusion on the opposite side, and a thoracentesis is done. Which finding afterward should concern the nurse MOST?
options: Equal chest expansion on both sides
Respiratory rate of 20 breaths per minute
Diminished breath sounds on the punctured side
Mild soreness at the puncture site
questions.rationale: After thoracentesis, diminished breath sounds, dyspnea, retractions, rising respiratory rate, or cyanosis on the affected side can mean a pneumothorax and must be reported.
explanations: Equal expansion is a normal finding.
A rate of 20 is within normal limits.
Correct: this may indicate a pneumothorax.
Mild soreness at the puncture site is expected.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 376)
questions.quote: diminished breath sounds, or cyanosis, which could indicate pneumothorax.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client in an acute asthma attack had loud wheezes on arrival. An hour later the nurse can barely hear any breath sounds, and the client is still struggling to breathe. How should the nurse interpret this?
options: Severe obstruction with impending respiratory failure
A good response to the bronchodilator therapy
Lower anxiety with slower, quieter breathing
questions.rationale: Wheezing needs moving air. Breath sounds that fade while distress continues mean airflow is severely blocked, a sign of impending respiratory failure.
explanations: Correct: a silent chest in a distressed client is an emergency.
Resolution would come with easier breathing, not ongoing distress.
Improvement would show less effort and better air entry.
The client is still in distress, so this is not calming.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 184)
questions.quote: Noticeably diminished breath sounds are an indication of severe obstruction and impending respiratory failure.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: During a home visit, a client with COPD on oxygen at 2 L/min by concentrator reports more shortness of breath than usual. The respiratory rate is 22. What should the nurse do FIRST?
options: Raise the oxygen flow to 6 L/min
Explain that this is expected with COPD
questions.rationale: The nurse gathers more data first. Oxygen is not increased without a prescription because clients with COPD can retain carbon dioxide; calling for transfer is premature.
explanations: Higher oxygen can depress the breathing drive in COPD and needs a prescription.
Correct: more assessment is needed before acting.
False reassurance ignores a change in condition.
Premature: the client is not yet shown to be in severe distress.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 186)
questions.quote: Oxygen is not increased without the approval of the primary health care provider, especially because the client with COPD can retain carbon dioxide.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client is admitted in sickle cell crisis. Which intervention is the nurse's PRIORITY?
questions.rationale: Hypoxemia drives red cells to sickle, so oxygen comes first, and airway and breathing take priority over circulation. Fluids and analgesics follow.
explanations: Hydration is important but follows oxygenation.
Pain relief is essential but is not the first priority.
Transfusion is not the first-line priority action.
Correct: oxygen addresses the hypoxemia causing sickling.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 339)
questions.quote: The priority nursing intervention for a client in sickle cell crisis is to administer supplemental oxygen

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which statement by a client discharged with a permanent pacemaker shows correct understanding of self-care?
options: 'I will check my pulse every day and report any change.'
'We have to give away our microwave oven.'
'I should stop using the electric fan at home.'
'I can never travel by airplane again.'
questions.rationale: Clients with pacemakers learn to take their pulse accurately and report changes in rate or rhythm. Grounded household appliances in good repair are safe, and air travel is allowed after informing security.
explanations: Correct: daily pulse checks detect pacemaker problems.
Grounded appliances in good repair are safe.
Household fans are safe to use.
Air travel is allowed; the client shows the pacemaker ID card at security.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 345)
questions.quote: Clients with permanent pacemakers must be able to take their pulse in the wrist and/or neck accurately

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with acute pericarditis has sharp chest pain that worsens on deep breathing. Which position should the nurse help the client into for comfort?
options: Flat on the back with one pillow
questions.rationale: Pericarditis pain worsens when lying supine and eases when sitting up and leaning forward, which reduces pressure on the inflamed pericardium.
explanations: Lying down worsens pericardial pain.
Side-lying does not relieve pericardial friction.
The supine position intensifies the pain.
Correct: sitting and leaning forward eases the pain.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 405)
questions.quote: severe precordial chest pain that intensifies when lying supine and decreases in a sitting position

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: After angioplasty of the iliac artery, which assessment BEST detects bleeding from the procedure site?
options: Asking the client to rate the pain
questions.rationale: Bleeding from the iliac artery collects in the retroperitoneal space, which shows as increasing abdominal girth. Pulses and capillary refill show patency and perfusion, not hidden bleeding.
explanations: Pedal pulses show arterial patency.
Correct: retroperitoneal bleeding increases abdominal girth.
Mild discomfort is expected and is not a direct measure.
Capillary refill reflects distal perfusion, not hidden bleeding.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 489)
questions.quote: Bleeding after iliac artery angioplasty causes blood to accumulate in the retroperitoneal area.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which solution should the nurse prepare for continuous bladder irrigation after a transurethral resection of the prostate (TURP)?
questions.rationale: Isotonic sterile normal saline is used. Sterile water can be absorbed systemically and cause hemolysis and kidney failure; dextrose solutions are not instilled into the bladder.
explanations: Correct: isotonic saline is used for CBI.
Hypotonic water can be absorbed and cause hemolysis.
Dextrose solutions are not introduced into the bladder.
Dakin's solution is a hypochlorite wound irrigant.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 391)
questions.quote: Continuous bladder irrigation is done after TURP using sterile normal saline, which is isotonic.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client's total serum calcium is 7.5 mg/dL. Which assessment finding should the nurse expect?
options: Shortened QT interval on the ECG
questions.rationale: A calcium level below 9 mg/dL is hypocalcemia, which increases neuromuscular excitability: twitching, tetany, hyperactive reflexes, positive Trousseau's and Chvostek's signs, and a prolonged QT interval.
explanations: Reflexes are hyperactive in hypocalcemia.
Constipation is linked to hypercalcemia.
Hypocalcemia prolongs the QT interval.
Correct: carpal spasm with a BP cuff shows neuromuscular irritability.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 527)
questions.quote: Hypocalcemia is a total serum calcium level less than 9 mg/dL (2.25 mmol/L).

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with acute kidney injury is on a fluid restriction of 1,500 mL per day. Which nursing measure helps the client keep to this restriction?
options: Keep a full water pitcher at the bedside
Offer ice chips and lip balm for thirst
questions.rationale: Ice chips and lip ointment ease thirst, and removing the pitcher helps compliance. Alcohol-based mouthwash dries the mucosa, and salty food increases thirst.
explanations: A visible pitcher encourages drinking beyond the limit.
Correct: ice chips and lip balm relieve thirst within the limit.
Alcohol dries the mouth and worsens thirst.
Salty food increases thirst.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 412)
questions.quote: The use of ice chips and lip ointments is another intervention that may be helpful to the client on fluid restriction.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Before starting a continuous IV infusion for a dehydrated client, which baseline data is MOST important for monitoring the client's fluid status?
questions.rationale: Daily weights compared against a baseline are the most sensitive and specific indicator of fluid volume change. The other data are useful but less precise.
explanations: Electrolytes are useful but do not measure volume change directly.
Correct: weight is the most sensitive indicator of fluid volume status.
I&O records are often incomplete and less precise.
Specific gravity reflects concentration, not total volume.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 1380)
questions.quote: body weight is a sensitive and specific indicator of fluid volume status

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A wound culture grows methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA). Which precautions should the nurse put in place?
questions.rationale: Contact precautions (standard precautions plus gloves and gown) are used for draining wounds, diarrhea, and methicillin-resistant infections.
explanations: Airborne precautions are for TB, measles, and varicella.
Droplet precautions are for organisms spread by large droplets, such as influenza.
Correct: MRSA in a wound spreads by direct and indirect contact.
Reverse isolation protects an immunosuppressed client.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 610)
questions.quote: Contact precautions are used for clients who have diarrhea, draining wounds, or methicillin-resistant infections.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client on chemotherapy is admitted on neutropenic precautions. Which action by the nurse is appropriate?
options: Put a vase of fresh flowers in the room
Room the client with a postoperative client
Serve fresh fruit salad at lunch
Have the client wear a mask outside the room
questions.rationale: A neutropenic client is placed in a private room and wears a mask whenever leaving it. Fresh flowers and raw fruit can carry organisms.
explanations: Fresh flowers and plants can harbor organisms.
The client needs a private room.
Raw fruit and vegetables can carry microorganisms.
Correct: a mask protects the client outside the room.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 696)
questions.quote: The client should wear a mask for protection from exposure to microorganisms whenever he or she leaves the room.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with cervical cancer returns from having a radiation implant inserted. Which action is the nurse's PRIORITY?
options: Assign the client to a private room
Place the client on protective isolation
Encourage her children to visit often
questions.rationale: A client with a radiation implant is placed in a private room with limited visitors to reduce others' exposure. Pregnant women and anyone under 16 should not visit, and bed rest keeps the implant in place.
explanations: Correct: a private room limits others' radiation exposure.
Others, not the client, need protection.
Children under 16 should not visit.
Bed rest is maintained to keep the implant in place.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 741)
questions.quote: The client who has a radiation implant is placed in a private room and has limited visitors.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with multiple myeloma is receiving IV hydration at 100 mL per hour. Which finding BEST shows the treatment is working?
questions.rationale: Hydration protects the kidneys from protein, calcium, and uric acid precipitating in the tubules. Creatinine is the most accurate measure of renal function.
explanations: Weight gain may mean fluid overload, not success.
Respiratory rate is unrelated to the goal of hydration.
Correct: a normal creatinine shows protected kidney function.
Blood pressure does not measure renal protection.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 458)
questions.quote: Creatinine is the most accurate measure of renal function.
